correctness.rationale: For every nonzero trace-zero complex 2x2 matrix, Hermitian parts are traceless. Cayley--Hamilton gives ||Re(e^{-it}T)||^2 as a scalar quadratic in sine and cosine. Its constant term is F^2/4; amplitude is |det T|/2, hence normalized amplitude rho=2|det T|/F^2. Positive angular averaging gives the exact formula. Strict convexity or concavity of x^(p/2), symmetry in rho, and explicit endpoints yield all inequalities and equality cases, with \\(p=2\\) constant. 512 exact rational matrix-moment and 24 numerical diagnostics passed. No finite check is used as a proof for continuum p.

value.rationale: For the recently introduced p-Cartesian operator norm, the natural fixed-Hilbert--Schmidt extremal problem on the first nontrivial traceless matrix class is solved completely: a determinant-ratio formula, sharp constants, a unique critical exponent \\(p=2\\), and exact nilpotent-versus-normal equality classes. It quantifies precisely how nonnormality changes a rotationally averaged operator norm; a rank-one \\(p=2\\) computation or general numerical-radius comparison alone cannot supply this classification.
